cohort: The study included 792,130 children who were Department of Defense TRICARE beneficiaries, born between October 1, 2001, and September 30, 2013, and continuously enrolled from within 35 days of birth until at least age 1 year, excluding those with an initial birth stay greater than 7 days or an allergic condition diagnosis within the first 6 months of life.
finding: The study found significant associations between the use of acid-suppressive medications (H2RAs and PPIs) and antibiotics during the first 6 months of infancy and the subsequent development of various allergic diseases in early childhood.
